Advances: ancora.review

Severity: Medium (calibrated). Follow-up from the /ship-it critical review (consolidated finding F16) and from the ancora-ayj cold verify.

Problem: the spec.review artifact embeds each changed file complete diff once per affected subject PLUS once under All files. Measured on this branch: 1105 diff articles for 175 distinct files, exactly 8 copies each, 9.65 MB, 301,143 DOM nodes, 5 second reload. Mechanism is lib/ancora/review.ex:137-143, where supporting is derived from the GLOBAL changed_files list for every subject, filtered only by source_file?/1, never consulting that subject derived footprint.

Why this ticket is needed now: F16 used to be a contract violation with a citable line, because ancora.review.code_pivot_grouping said clause-level hunk. Ticket ancora-ayj correctly rewrote that line to describe what the code actually does (there is no hunk-slicing anywhere in the module, so the old wording described something never built). That was the honest fix and it is merged. The side effect is that F16 lost its written basis, and nothing replaces it: ancora.review.size_budget bounds renderer SOURCE lines (5,000 across lib/ancora/review/ plus lib/ancora/markdown.ex), not artifact bytes. Today the artifact could reach 50 MB and the gate would stay green.

Deliverable, recommended verbatim by the cold verifier: add a must to ancora.review alongside size_budget that bounds the rendered ARTIFACT rather than the renderer source. Suggested wording: the rendered artifact shall include each changed file diff at most twice (once under the subject that owns it, once under All files), and shall stay under N MB for a change set of 200 files, enforced by a standing test. Pair it with a scenario building a multi-subject fixture that asserts the per-file article count, so the test FAILS today and passes once supporting changes are scoped to the owning subject. Note size_budget own cut list already names the right lever (supporting-changes hunks degrade to a file-link list); it was simply wired to the source-line budget instead of an artifact budget.

Knock-on already observed: every id=file- exists 8 times, so the watched-card defining-file link resolves to a copy inside a display:none pivot and the page does not move when clicked (consolidated finding F38, same ticket).

Cannot land on the epic branch: this needs a new must plus a failing-then-passing standing test and a behavior change to subject scoping, which is a contract decision beyond the scope of the blocker fixes the ship was waiting on.

Verification:
- Tests to pass: a new standing test in test/ancora/review_test.exs (or test/ancora/static/review_budget_test.exs) building a multi-subject fixture and asserting the per-file diff article count and unique id=file- anchors, tagged to the new ancora.review requirement; existing tagged tests under ancora.review
- Behaviors to demonstrate: (1) new must in ancora.review next to size_budget bounding the rendered ARTIFACT: each changed file's diff appears at most twice (owning subject plus All files) and a 200-file change set stays under the stated MB ceiling; (2) the new test FAILS on the pre-change code (prove it in the IMPLEMENTED comment) and passes after supporting changes are scoped to the owning subject's derived footprint; (3) every id=file- anchor is unique so the watched-card defining-file link scrolls the page (F38)

  - Verifier tier: mix spec.check --base the epic base sha recorded at admission plus tagged and --stale selections only; do NOT run the full suite.
- Standing bounce-class checks:
  - Production call site named for each new callable surface, with the proving test that exercises that production path.
  - Fixture hygiene: one TmpGitRepo per test, no shared temp dirs, async only where the fixture allows.
  - Spec surfaces kept fresh for every touched callable surface. Drift, growth, and shrink clear only through substantive requirement or scenario edits in the same diff, never through a Spec-Ack trailer.
  - Every conditional clause covered by a test.

Reasoning: The verifier's Gap is real and I reproduced it from my own fixture. A watched card carries the FULL file diff, not a hunk: lib/ancora/review.ex:237 sets `lines: Map.get(diffs, file, [])` on every acknowledged card and lib/ancora/review.ex:180 does the same for drift cards, and lib/ancora/review/html.ex:201-216 renders that through the same `diff/1` used by the All files article. Nothing dedupes cards across subjects, so a changed public definition called by S subjects renders S+1 copies. The headline win is not in dispute and I re-measured it: rendering this repo's own change set at 6852200 gives 286,636 bytes, 11 file articles, 7 file-* anchors all unique, 0 duplicates.

Reproduced independently: I wrote my own fixture generator (N subjects, each with a spec, a private module, and a tagged test; all N tests also call `Fixture.Shared.value/0`), committed a base, then changed ONLY the shared module's def line to `def value, do: :changed`, ran the real `Review.build/2` and `Html.render/1`, and counted occurrences of the added line text. Two subjects: 3 copies, 2 watched articles, 1 subject-level file article, 1 anchor id, 2 hrefs. Three subjects: 4 copies, 3 watched articles. Four subjects: 5 copies, 4 watched articles. The scaling claim is right, S+1, and the anchor stays unique at every N. Note the shared file gets ZERO subject-level `<article class="file">` at every N, so the new must is satisfied while the diff body fanouts. On this repo's real change set the artifact currently renders 0 watched cards, so the residual is latent here, not biting today.

The must as written: ".spec/specs/ancora.review.spec.md:126 — 'The rendered artifact shall include no more than one subject-level file-diff article for each changed file in addition to its All files article, and every `file-*` anchor shall be unique. A standing 200-file fixture shall render to less than 1 MB.'" The verifier's reading is correct and the decision record removes any doubt: .spec/decisions/ancora.decision.review_artifact_contract.md states in the same paragraph both that "The Code pivot describes full changed-file diffs for watched cards" and that "Each changed file has no more than one subject-level file-diff article". The boundary was drawn around `<article class="file">` deliberately, leaving `<article class="watched">` unbounded. The line is true of the code and false of the ticket's proves line.

The standing test: test/ancora/review_test.exs:199 cannot reach the fanout case, and the verifier is right about why. `changed_definitions/2` at lib/ancora/review.ex:302 matches only def/defmacro/defguard/defdelegate on add or del lines, so the fixture's `@changed true` yields no binding and therefore no watched card for the shared file, which the test's own card assertion confirms. Alpha and beta each get a definition change but each is called by one subject only. One correction to the verifier: it wrote that both tests count only `<article class="file">`, and that is not accurate for review_test.exs:199, which asserts `count_occurrences(html, changed_line) == 2` on raw diff text and WOULD catch a watched-card copy. The test misses because of the fixture shape, not the counting method. Conclusion unchanged. The verifier is right about test/ancora/static/review_budget_test.exs:79, which sets `watched_interface: []` on every generated subject, so the 1 MB ceiling has never been tested against card fanout.

Disclosure: fair reading, and I would not push it further than the verifier did. The IMPLEMENTED comment claims "the defining 'one' clause has a shared-footprint test", and that test's shared-module edit is the one arrangement in which the shared file produces no card. The residual should have been named. It reads as a coverage claim the implementer believed rather than concealment, so treat it as a work-order item, not a character finding.

Remedy chosen and why: Option A. Option B would write the S+1 growth into the contract and hand back a ticket whose title is "review artifact size" and whose bound grows with callers. That guts the ticket. Option A costs little here because the deterministic owner already exists: `file_owners/1` at lib/ancora/review.ex:279 already maps each footprint file to exactly one subject via a sorted `Map.put_new` fold, and it is already threaded into `subjects/10`. Scoping the diff body to the owning card is a map lookup and a plain argument, no memo, registry, cache or process, and the net effect on the artifact is deletion. The link the card needs already exists: html.ex:209 emits the `href="#file-..."` that this ticket made unique, so a non-owning card is not losing information, it is losing a redundant copy of information one click away.

Does the remedy fit this ticket's Allowed touches: mostly yes, with one ruling. lib/ancora/review.ex and both spec files are squarely allowed. The html.ex half is a stretch: the ticket permits html.ex for anchor uniqueness only, with rendering defects belonging to ancora-xla.4. I am allowing it here, narrowly, because ancora-xla.4 has already merged so there is no open sibling to receive it, and because skipping the empty `<pre class="diff">` on a link-only card is the rendering half of THIS ticket's own contract line rather than a defect fix. The latitude is exactly one guard so an empty card does not render an empty black diff box. No markup, CSS, badge, severity or ARIA change beyond that.

Needs the repository owner: no. The remedy uses machinery that already exists and follows the ticket's stated purpose. The only judgment call is the html.ex latitude above, which I am making with reasons stated so the owner can veto it cheaply.

Bounce reason: bound the diff BODY, not the article class.
1. Rewrite ancora.review.artifact_size so it bounds copies of a changed file's diff regardless of element class. Wording to the effect of: the rendered artifact shall include each changed file's diff body at most twice, once under the single subject that owns the file and once in the All files section; every `file-*` anchor shall be unique and every defining-file link shall target it. Update the matching paragraph in .spec/decisions/ancora.decision.review_artifact_contract.md, which currently states the watched-card carve-out explicitly.
2. In lib/ancora/review.ex, give each watched file exactly one diff-carrying card. Reuse `file_owners/1` where the file is in a footprint; for any card whose file is not, fall back to the first subject in sorted id order that carries a card for that file, so the rule is total and deterministic. Non-owning cards keep binding, badge and file link, and carry `lines: []`. Do not add state, a registry, a cache or a process; a fold over the already-sorted subject list is enough.
3. In lib/ancora/review/html.ex, make `watched_card/1` omit the `<pre class="diff">` block when `lines` is empty. That is the whole permitted rendering change.
4. Replace the fanout scenario's fixture with the case that actually fanouts: a shared module whose public DEFINITION changes, called by THREE tagged subjects. Assert the added definition line appears exactly twice in the rendered artifact, that three defining-file links resolve to the one `file-*` id, and that all three cards still render with their badges. Keep a non-definition assertion too if you want, but it does not carry the clause.
5. Fix test/ancora/static/review_budget_test.exs:79, which sets `watched_interface: []` on every subject. Populate watched cards in the 200-file fixture so the 1 MB ceiling is tested against card fanout. While there, align the fixture with the scenario text: the scenario says "one short added line each" and the fixture uses 1,000-character lines.
6. In the new IMPLEMENTED comment, state the measured copy count for the three-subject definition-change fixture before and after, and say plainly that the previous round's shared-footprint test did not reach this case.
Advisory, not blocking: `derive_subjects/3` at lib/ancora/review.ex:244 ends in a bare `_error -> {%{}, %{}}`, which silently empties every subject's supporting changes, test changes and acknowledged cards with no finding raised. It did not fire here. If a cheap finding fits in this diff, take it; otherwise file it.
